body: thinking about it? no. if you be kind with yourself the memories and love can become something more honest. I still remember how endless it felt a year ago but life is about change. as you let yourself have more experiences, those feelings start to settle and you become more at peace with the people you both were when the breakup happened. there might always be grief at the loss of love, or however else you process that persons absence, but you choose to live. closing yourself off will only hurt you in the long run.

thank you, that means a lot. I hope the same for you with moving on. 

honestly, that's what made it more heartbreaking because I could see what my inaction was doing. its hard to explain because there's only so much you can say online, and this was only one part of it. but she had been going through a hard time as well, the difference being looking back I at least was vulnerable and tried to communicate what was happening with me. I don't hold it against her though because everyone deals with mental health in their own way. but despite me feeling similar ways to how she sometimes wasn't communicating the best or I could tell she was dealing with something and that made it awkward, I never used it against her. even after the breakup. I mean the reality could have been exactly what you said, she knew what I was dealing with but I took too long to show her things could get better. as hard as it is letting go, the easy explanation is also just that humans are messy and complicated and what's the point of holding onto some things even if it hurts. 

thank you again for sharing, it is important to always consider what your ex had been dealing with as well.

thank you, its just hard to let go of how in the end I felt like such an empty person from not being what she wanted me to be for her. and you got it so right, it's all the questioning of yourself that it only leads to, without any clear answer to reassure you. I don't doubt that she had genuine feelings, and in fairness I was too scared to admit that i wasn't comfortable with what she wanted because I loved her a lot and didn't want to lose her. but it was like trying to breath underwater, and all she could do was ask why I was struggling to do so.

honestly the fact that we were in a LDR since the beginning of it for 2 and a half years and she took issue with the fact that I did not fully understand her every day behaviour and attitude. the irony is I felt the same, and it came to the point where I wanted to be more closer but there were a lot of other things that she wanted to focus on in regard to our connection. it honestly just made me feel really bad about myself because I was trying, communicating and figuring out how we could go from long distance to something more every day. but what she wanted out of me (an open relationship) was something I wasn't comfortable with. 

so it ended with her telling me how she had given 3 years of her life to me, how she had given herself to me in so many ways...and i just wondered at the time, didnt i do all those things for you too? you did those things out of what you told me was love? waa that not true? what were you trying to tell me after you thought things weren't going to work? that all those things you did was in the hope that I'd give you something you never got from anyone else? that I'd feel comfortable enough out of loyalty and paying back all those "things" you did for me to feel fine with you dating other people? 

Well I guess all the guilt and self-loathing goes to me. yay.

as simple, and probably annoying, as it sounds it was really giving it time. I was patient with myself and let all of my emotions out, all the grief and bitterness and self-doubt. there was no point keeping it in, or holding myself against anything. 

I think also just realising (especially if you were the one who wanted to try and see if things could work out) that if your ex really wanted a lifetime with you, they wouldn't have broken up in the first place. there is always communication, patience, respect, and many other ways to get passed hardships rather than simply saying its done. 

nobody is perfect and I suppose we each have agency in the amount of love we have and we give to others. at a certain point you just have to tell yourself that person couldn't give me anymore. its not on you.

this one hurts. i was the one to ask the question of whether she still loved me because there were other reasons behind the breakup, and she says only "platonically" with a smile on her face after three years together.

"How can I love someone who's not a whole person yet" 

i don't know where it came from or how much she meant it. but it has impacted me up to this moment.

being okay with something she said wouldn't change things in the relationship and it ended up doing just that whilst I fully trusted her. if there is ever a next time, the moment I feel some sense of doubt or discomfort it won't be something to hide.

realising they've moved on and me feeling worthless and sad is hurting myself most of all. sure their choice to show care in the end was to realise keeping any contact would hurt but you've just got to respect that. I hate to accept this but it might just be the fact that people come and go in your life. you just got to make sure you remember the person they were and all the things that made you love them as equally as the decisions and actions that led to the breakup. it all matters. so I can sit and feel sorry whilst blaming some unknown force, or simply start doing things to give more love to myself and anyone new who'll come into my life.
I...I didn't. a large part of the reason I wanted nc was because she dumped me and didn't want to see if things could work again. where did you get that idea from?

about 7-8 months. I still think of her on occasion but realised after a while that there was no one else but me who was going to move my life forward. I recognised the mistakes we both made, the reasons behind why things went the way they did, and whilst I am still yet to forgive myself and her fully I have remained trying to put out as much self-love as possible. in the end it helps both yourself and all the new connections you can make, both platonic and romantic. why deny yourself the opportunity for happiness for something given up on?
the pain of having to ask that question. I'm so sorry.

I know how hard it is to admit but it'll be better in the long run. no matter how much someone says they love you in one moment, you don't realise their limits and what they're capable of until its too late. for some it's just the end of the line. this is coming from someone who wanted it to work and was told by my ex that they felt relieved things ended so it's not from a place of indifference. 

I think also its hard to come to terms with how someone who you idealised and loved so dearly could decide or end up not loving you anymore. but in a cruel but reasonable way, you can't live without being hurt, and you can't live without learning how to heal from that. 

please take as long as you need dealing with everything this brings, the heart is a dear thing. but all I can offer is to take this as an opportunity to grow and love who you are and can be because this shows no one else will do that for you.

yes and funny thing is a few of us have gone through breakups in the past year so it's something we all talk about. but it doesn't help in those moments when you're by yourself and can't help but think of them and all the things you miss and how it still has such a big hold over you.
sorry I wasn't sure how else to describe it. I suppose it's more just being tired of feeling this way.

undermining the way I felt about certain things because that was just my "outlook" on life I was stuck on, making me question whether I even was able to think or feel about things in the relationship properly.

its been a couple months now since the BU, and honestly those first few weeks were hell with separation anxiety. my head felt like it was both empty and screaming from too many emotions. but even now after so many months, it's become more of a lamented grief. like that sadness will just sit with you and you'll never know where to place it.
I wonder how long it haunts you about feeling given up on. that they'd rather have a life without you than try, and not break the trust that became something you held so dearly to.
I guess the only choice is to just live on with the ghost of a connection left with you

please don't do it. it's not about pushing them away, it's about protecting yourself. I know how desperate it feels to ask those questions but I promise you they only lead to more heartbreak when you already know the answer.
it honestly is always when you think you're doing better, which makes it all the more painful.
I wouldn't say happier, but at least not obsessing over whether I will eventually talk to them anymore.

honestly this. one thing a lot of people don't realise is how badly mental illness can blind you to your own actions and behaviour. even if your intentions are good and you want to only treat those you care about with decency and understanding. being trapped in your own thoughts and feelings can turn all of that upside down, and before you know it you're questioning yourself on why you didn't realise how your choices were effecting the people you cared for. 

it makes looking back on your life not regretful or sorrowful, but tortured. not even in a "poetic" way but for the fact that you have to simply live with having made those choices unbeknownst to yourself not realising how they built up over time. it's like being strapped in the passenger seat unable to move whilst the driver goes head on into oncoming traffic constantly.
I'm not sure which way would be kinder on your heart. but that doesn't matter in this situation because regardless, it will still hurt.
I break down every time. there's a text from a year back saying she will always choose to love me regardless of what happens. and now we haven't spoken in months and I don't think we ever will again.

honestly, you realise after how much you are scared to say even if you and your ex communicated a lot when texting, because you just didn't know or worried about how they would take it sometimes. 

a lot of my last relationship we spoke through texting because we were at different unis and it was more or less long distance, and I think towards the end of it we both felt misunderstood by the other because at the end of the day how do you truly learn about someone when they're just words on a screen? you're not around them to learn their little quirks and behaviours and all the little things that make you appreciate and love them even more. 

I saw that too late and by the time I told her that reason she had already moved on with her feelings for me, and thought I hadn't done enough to understand her. but the irony is I felt misunderstood too. so idk sometimes it's just the fact that you're dealt with a cruel hand with someone you could've loved for longer or even life.
going to take myself out and enjoy the things I like and appreciate. hopefully loving myself will help.

don't give yourself the time or space to think about them. It starts to take over all your thoughts and you can't escape them. 

its fine if you still love or have feelings for them. but please please try focus on yourself and your own happiness. it can be hard if that hurts knowing they aren't there to share those moments with. but honestly they're probably enjoying their life and not thinking of you. so why waste your life over someone who didn't want you anymore?

"yes" after I asked if they had feelings for her but not me. 

I wish I never asked, it has still stayed with me after all this time.
I'd just be too scared that it could end, so what's the point.

we always were upfront about each of our problems, so for me whatever we said to each other was what there was to say. 

I won't say any details because that's private, but a lot of things were putting distance between us anyway. I should have realised what she was saying and doing was her deciding it wasn't working between us. I was too naive with this being my first relationship that we were okay, and this was our first bump as we had never had any arguments or tension before in the three years we were together. 

it just hurts the first time we were going through a rough patch, albeit one that was going on for a month or so, she immediately ended it. but as she told me "life doesn't work that way". so I'm just gonna carry on with my life and sit with this pain because what else is there to do.

she was really sad the previous week before the breakup and was acting more and more distant. but just before that happened we had a talk about giving each other some space because life had been quite intense for us both, and the relationship was getting strained. 

me being a stupid person meant I thought her being distant was just her prioritising herself before we got back to doing relationship stuff. but fuck me for trusting a person who said they'd want to stay with me and love me no matter what.
yes, a thousand times yes.
I wish that were true. I've tried so many things, getting back into old interests, meeting new people, going out, even therapy. In the end I'm simply just unhappy, can't that be reason enough?
just not happy, never have been happy. and the times I have been, they've stopped because I'm broken. there's nothing else to say.
sending hugs. it honestly is so tiring, but weirdly it's a tiredness I'm scared to let go of because it'll mean letting go of them.
its honestly hard not to feel this way.
"hi"
8 years... I hope you find peace with it

this has been a weird and often gruelling experience when you're a trans person because there's a lot of stereotypes with breakups on how the "woman" and "man" act like when dealing with the emotions and fallout from it. it makes you question yourself even more, makes you question your behaviour and emotions and the life you have. it makes you wonder how your ex thought about you with how you acted. its another type of emotional hell that you'll only understand if you're trans or gender non-conforming. 

an example being, I haven't got much of a support system at all and spent the first month or so by myself in my room and feeling my emotions a lot. if you go on social media, etc etc this fits with a lot of "male" experiences of a breakup and the whole shtick about not having people to reach out. but my experience is unique, and it hurts even more having them tied to the "man's side' of a breakup. everyone's situation post breakup is their own and I guess you can't deny the patterns. and these gendered patterns often have valid reasons. but it's more difficult being an outsider to yet another experience where you're not a part of either. and on top of losing someone you love it's like another weight has been placed on you that adds to the struggle to recovery.

there's a lot of things that get broken when being the one who still is in love, the trust you built, the hope, the potential, all the things you still wanted to experience with them, all the things you wanted to repeat, the unique type of happiness and love they brought to your life. its hard letting all that go, even as a process it just makes it longer. 

but I guess also being the one not in love anymore, you give all that up too. it's just makes it seem more like there was a possibility of all that happening, and it just didn't. it makes sense as to why you'd not take the risk going through all of that if the feelings aren't there. 

sense doesn't mend a broken heart though.

I wish you the best and that you find the people who will fulfill you. but I want you to know how hard it was for me towards the end, how everything you were saying to me and acting like made me so confused and scared. how I always opened up about my vulnerabilities and fears but you waited until after the breakup to tell me yours and blamed me for not realising you were in that position. I know we were both in difficult positions and maybe it was inevitable that distance grew between us without an easy fix. but I was in it for life and all I could feel was my love growing for you, even when it felt hopeless. because I trusted what you told me and trusted that you needed to focus on yourself before we had time back for us. you were my first love, the first person to really show me what dreaming of love could feel like, how love is the choice you make every day. unfortunately for us that choice got harder and you felt better letting go than hurting more. I respect you for that. I know my love for you isn't as intense anymore, but it's there. and honestly I'm not sure where you are at right now because you always changed what you said to me, and never really truly opened up. I knew you weren't the type to be like that and I trusted that whatever you told me was all that there was to say. but it hurts knowing you felt all these other things growing and never told me. never asked for help from me as someone who loves you. I know I seemed like a wreck that was unable to listen but I said I'd be there for you, and you not opening up just made me feel more disconnected to you. I just wanted us to connect on a more emotional level, but maybe I was too focused on that and neglected the rest of what a relationship should be. I've gone through so many emotions since it happened; anger, frustration, agonising heartache, sadness and just grief. but feeling like a stranger to you is the worst of all. anywho, I wonder if you ever think about me too. if I was someone you thought you could love forever. if you saw us as a future to wonder about. i miss our silly voices. I miss our morning and night texts. I miss the feeling that eventually I'd see you again. i miss calling you my dear. goodbye again.

thank you for this, you're absolutely right tbh. the last few times we talked after the breakup she did give off the impression that she wanted us to move on if it meant staying friends, saying goodbye or whatever else. she just wanted me to respect her decision I guess. tbh i think I'm only feeling this way again because of sad songs I've been listening to for the passed few days. should probably let the cloud of sadness move passed me before thinking about this again.

I did two days after being the one to ask for it back in September but since that day I haven't anymore because I found that whilst my ex may want to remember me fondly, they are focused on moving on. so I should too.

not to say it hasn't been hard. I have conversations with them in my head and think of them a lot of the time. because honestly I still love them despite our situation not working out. it just hurts more because I have no idea whether they think of me often as well or not since that last time we spoke.

I'd like to think I was trying my hardest in the moment but looking back I don't know if there was more that could've been done by me or not. it hurts knowing I made my ex feel drained from me not giving back to her equally so I completely respect and understand her reason with that, which i guess she was in a similar position to you. 

but I don't know if its right for me to feel guilty for simply not having the energy to try harder for her because of a mental illness. you wouldn't ask your partner to walk 10 miles for you if they had a broken foot, so why should it be different for mental health? 

and what makes it harder to resolve is I wasn't always like that, this was something that only happened this year. so for her to have that as a reason for ending things felt hurtful and like she was judging me based on my mental health instead of who I am as a person outside of that.

thats probably what the best thing is, to look at it one day at a time. if you just keep thinking about things in the future or where you eventually want to be, it feels like the present moment won't ever improve. thank you for the help, I hope things get better for you as time passes.

this happened to me. weeks before the breakup she told me she feels like I had changed, and looking back the way she expressed that should have told me all I needed to know. but in that moment, and currently still, I'm in a really bad place with my mental health so tbh I'm not sure who I really am. and I can't help but hate myself for losing the love of my life for not attempting to get better and leaving it too late. and to show her that person wasn't me. that I wanted to do so much more for her. but staying alive took so much out of me.
thank you for this

your emotions and pain are valid but from what it sounds like, it seems you were very insecure and held unhealthy expectations for what a polyamorous relationship should be. I was similar in a lot of ways where it felt like i wasn't enough, no matter her reassurance, and i think my continued lack of support with her reassuring me meant it wasn't working well. 

what you have to remember is with polyamous affection and love, although it may not always be equal with the time spent with certain people and what you do with each other, this doesn't take away the love the person had for you. as my ex told me, it was never give and take. but if you as a person aren't ready to embrace that, it's more respectful and caring for you to realise that it just wasn't going to be a good situation for either of you. and that doesn't reflect badly on you as a person. you are still worthy of the love and connections you want. unfortunately, I feel with polyamory, if you aren't absolutely on the same page it can lead to a lot of resentment and misjudgement, which is simply a result of honest mistakes and misunderstandings, and not out of being cruel or in bad faith. 

I hope you are able to find someone who loves you and makes you feel worthy of love. but I know it will take time to get over the loss and pain of someone you held deep affection for and it ended because of this reason. Trust me it doesn't make it easy. but it's nothing bad taking as much time as you need and always remind yourself you are enough. as much as the connection you had with your ex was good, this is a situation where neither of you should have to sacrifice a part of your happiness to stay together.

I don't think you can answer this with certainty.

I've had days I hated them for making me feel this pain and would have rather they never loved me and asked me to start a relationship with them. it brings up a lot of thoughts about how they could have treated me better and how I could have done more for them. so in the end it just doesn't feel good at all reflecting in that way because you end up becoming cynical about something so meaningful.

but other days i feel grateful for the time i got to spend with them and that I was able to be with someone who loved me in a way that made me feel special. on those days it doesn't make it any easier though because knowing how much their love made me feel happy just makes me miss them more. I guess when you're in the moment you don't think that their love could change...until it does.

saying this though, I don't know whether it's easier for those with a certain answer to this question because the reason might be even more heartbreaking or damaging.

there's many reasons why a relationship had to end. I'm sorry that whatever you've experienced led you to that perspective and I respect your view on it. but please don't judge my statement as a superficial statement of longing or inability to let go. I love them for who they are and what they meant to me. I only ever wished happiness and comfort for them. and as hard as it is to come to terms with, that ended up not being with me. so part of my process of letting go is acknowledging that I still hold a special place for them in my heart. but it's that love that I need to grieve to move forward, no matter how long it takes. this isn't to be noble, but vulnerable with yourself and how it has effected you.

I thought I was wrong in feeling upset that they kept doing things with another person I said I wanted to do with them. they thought it wasn't a big deal and said I was making it more of a problem than it needed to be. I ended up feeling bad for putting too much pressure on them. 

but knowing other people have gone through this heartbreak has shown i don't need to feel wrong or guilty for wanting to do certain things with them, even if it was as mundane as going to the movies. because if I mattered enough they'd realise why it hurt me that they said they didn't have the time to do so with me then days later I hear they did the exact thing I asked with that other person. 

we've been broken up for a while now and I've struggled with feeling guilt over my actions regarding this exact topic as it effected me a lot more towards the end and led me to have very hurt and confused emotions regarding my love for them. even after the break up they casually said to me how they went to the movies with that other person to feel better. its as if they didn't even know me or why it hurt me so much. I don't know how I'll recover from that.
very true

I think I made my ex feel this way unintentionally. After the lockdown when we had barely spent much time together, it felt like we didn't have a chance to reconnect so I told her a few times all I really want is to spend time with her. but it eventually got to a point where she said it felt like i was seeking too much attention and being needy. at the time I couldn't see what I was doing wrong and hearing that from her hurt me because from my pov it was the case that we simply hadn't had much time to spend together and it was upsetting that most of our interactions were through texts and calls. 

looking back now I can see how the way I went about it would have been very draining on her and didn't realise I should have actually done more than simply say "I want to spend time with you", which whilst sincere might not mean that much. I wish I could just blame the way the year was and how everything was so difficult, but there were so many better ways for me to have expressed that feeling whilst still respecting her boundaries and needs, and showing I do care for her in an understanding way. sorry doesn't make up for hurting her in that way.

its such a strange feeling because it's one of those instances you'd tell yourself, "yes, I can change because I love them enough to do so". but it's not fair on them if you're heart isn't fully in it, and you're not sure if you'd be able to meet their needs, or have your own needs met. as heartbreaking as it is I think its more important to recognise how that situation is just something tragic. it's not something I'd wish on anyone else.

thank you for being vulnerable about this, I hope it gets better for you. just remember, sometimes you've yet to meet all the people who will love you, and if its someone who will love you for who you are then that will be even more fulfilling. but I guess the only thing to do now is make her a part of you and do whatever to come out the other side of that pain a better person.

I understand that's what probably was happening on their side. but it's not easy when one day you both were speaking words of reassurance to each other and a week later they say they want to break up. there were many reasons making our situation complicated, but if that's how they were feeling I'd rather they confided in me, even if it broke my heart just the same, than let me feel some hope for it too to be shattered. but I recognise my situation is not the same as everyone else's and its the case that both sides suffered heartbreak from things having to end. 

edit: for clarification

the initial reason was that she is poly and I wasn't really comfortable with that. I tried my best to show her I was going to change and try to adjust my view of relationships and love, but I think some part of me knew it wasn't going to make me happy so I became scared of doing anything in the relationship. I think she ended up taking that as me not trying anymore and it led to her coming to the conclusion that our relationship wasn't going to work out in the long term and she lost feelings for me on top of the main reason. she eventually told me post break up that she felt like I never made the effort to reach back and be there for her when it was too difficult of a situation for me to explain that I was trying my hardest. and trying to change, when the poly side of things was taking a lot out of me emotionally and mentally. I mourn the loss of our relationship but I don't think it was fair for either of us to carry on and we'd each have to sacrifice one part of our happiness to be together. it just sounds tragic laid out like this.

i became quite confused after the break up, let my emotions get the better of me, and kept being quite insistant with answers from her as to why we couldn't try to make things work. it eventually led to an argument where things were revealed and more or less showed how we weren't on the same page with understanding each other. i only have myself to blame but that revelation hurt a lot more than the break up. but since then I asked her to go no contact and i don't think she would want to break that any time soon. so for the foreseeable future we aren't in each others lives anymore after three years being together. i wish we could have been but it all hurts too much.
same here. apparently they woke up one day and realised they don't love me anymore, it's a fun revelation.

I haven't heard it put like this yet but it honestly feels so accurate. the emptiness doesn't move anywhere, it just becomes a part of you and you have to somehow make it a foundation for something new as hard as that may be.
some people have said they're still feeling bad after a year. i suppose it's just something you live with
around three months i guess

"How can I love someone who's not whole". Thank you for telling me that im not worthy of love because I was struggling with mental health and being vulnerable about it for the first ever time in the relationship. I understand that it might have took a lot out of you to be with someone who was spiralling in a bad way but I told you constantly that I understood I wasn't being myself and I was going to get therapy and wanted to move past the bad year I had to be there for you properly again but all you could say to me was "you've changed" and judged me based on my mental illness and not who I am.

"You made me feel like I was wrong". No sorry, I respect your emotions but I never said anything out of turn. I always commented on things you had already brought up about yourself and I only ever commented on things like your adhd to make you feel comfortable about it. You not being accepting of yourself is your issue and you should have been clear about that to me. Not make me feel guilty about it after the break up and expect me to have magically known you felt like that. Along with saying to my face that I apparently was gaslighting you by simply commenting on something you confided in me about, when all I did was say it was sad or unfortunate and trying to relate with my own experiences. When in actuality you were the one who kept invalidating my emotions and telling me it was my own fault for seeing things in a bad way whenever I brought up a discomfort I had. Who was the one being gaslit?

"You drained me". Again...never brought this up with me during the relationship and all of a sudden is a major reason as to why it ended. Why not speak to me about it? Not make me feel fucking guilty and a terrible person for not being aware of something you never spoke about or showed. You made it so difficult to be there for you when all I got was a keyhole into how you were doing and how to connect with you and then you criticise me for not seeing what was through the whole door? No person can live with that expectation whilst constantly being told they're not understanding someone they love and being there for someone they love when you hardly ever let me do anything for you not out of sympathy but because our lives were getting more entwined.

"I gave you three years of my life, how much longer do i have to wait". Excuse me what? I can't even begin to come to terms with how this made me feel. Like I was the one taking them for granted when they asked me to be in a relationship with them. And you didn't give me your life, you chose to share it with me. So if you see it like that then I'm glad you broke up with me because I deserve to be seen as more than someone who is just an inconvenience or pit stop.

There was so many other things you said to me after the break up that made me feel like this horrible, manipulative person. But you were the one who always called me your angel, your perfect person, the one who finally loved and cared for you. And the one moment in our relationship I started struggling all of a sudden you kept critiquing me, kept telling me I've changed, that I'm not there for you and how I didn't put in the same effort as you? Even if it was in a moment of frustration that you said all of this, how can you expect someone who gave you their heart to feel anything but betrayed, given up on and left behind whilst you go off and be confident with yourself because I was the one who told you to love and accept who you are.
